decisions.title: TypeScript + NestJS on Node 24 in all services
decisions.decision: All five services use TypeScript with NestJS on Node 24 LTS (.nvmrc, engines, CI, node:24-slim images, Cloud Run functions runtime nodejs24). Revised from Node 22.
decisions.why: One language lets packages/common serve every unit without duplication. Prism CLI 5.16 needs Node >= 24.18; Angular 20 and NestJS 11 support Node 24.
decisions.alternatives: Stay on Node 22 and pin Prism 5.14.
decisions.consequences: One runtime for the whole team. If nodejs24 were missing for Cloud Run functions in the region, functions alone fall back to nodejs22.

decisions.title: Angular 20 with SSR for the frontend
decisions.decision: Angular 20 with SSR on public routes, deployed as its own container.
decisions.why: Original plan choice for SSR on public pages.
decisions.consequences: Superseded by ADR-0007 (Next.js) before any Angular code existed.

decisions.title: Single monorepo with CI per affected folder
decisions.decision: One monorepo; CI workflows triggered per affected folder.
decisions.why: One branch per person and main always deployable.
decisions.consequences: Workflows in .github/workflows are path-filtered per unit; shared changes to packages/common trigger every dependent unit.

decisions.title: One GCP project aforo-dev-teamf in southamerica-east1
decisions.decision: Single GCP project aforo-dev-teamf (aforo-dev was taken globally) in southamerica-east1, billed to Julián's account.
decisions.why: One shared environment is enough for the slice.
decisions.consequences: Julián is the only one who can create the project and grant access; one shared dev environment that anyone can break (see RISK-02).

decisions.title: One Cloud SQL instance, one database and user per service
decisions.decision: A single Cloud SQL instance hosts one database and one user per Postgres service (catalog, orders, inventory).
decisions.why: Keeps Database per Service at the cost of one instance; the instance is turned off when nobody works.
decisions.consequences: Database per Service is enforced by separate databases/users, not instances; 25-connection limit must be budgeted (ADR-0005).

decisions.title: Simulated login issued by the Gateway
decisions.decision: The Gateway issues an HS256 JWT (8 h) from POST /api/v1/auth/login with email and displayName, no password; Identity Platform only if time allows.
decisions.why: Avoids managed identity setup in the slice; the token keeps OIDC claim shape so switching is configuration.
decisions.consequences: No real authentication; logic services trust Gateway headers. Way back: validate against JWKS in the Gateway and drop /auth/login.

decisions.title: Orders and Inventory do not verify the queue pass
decisions.decision: The queue returns an opaque passToken; it is forwarded as X-Queue-Pass and logged but never verified downstream. No JWKS, no ES256 signature, no key in Secret Manager.
decisions.why: Cut to fit the slice; the contract keeps the header as the hook for later verification.
decisions.alternatives: ES256-signed pass verified by Inventory (Entrega 3 ADR-04).
decisions.consequences: RD-04 is not met: any valid session can call /orders without the queue; the waiting room is a UI control, not a system control. RF-06 only partial. The E-02 dev run skipped the waiting room because of this.

decisions.title: No organizer UI
decisions.decision: There is no organizer UI; events are created by the seed and with Postman.
decisions.why: Not part of the purchase happy path in the acceptance script.
decisions.consequences: Catalog has no organizer roles; demo events are created by scripts and cannot be deleted (catalog has no delete).

decisions.title: Payment-gateway mock inside Orders
decisions.decision: The payment mock was planned as a module inside Orders.
decisions.why: Original plan simplicity.
decisions.consequences: Superseded by D-16: the mock moved to a separate Cloud Run function.

decisions.title: Everything lives in the cloud; no full local stack
decisions.decision: The full stack is never run locally; each person runs only their unit against cloud dependencies.
decisions.why: Avoid maintaining a local copy of the whole platform.
decisions.consequences: Slow feedback loop mitigated with Prism mocks (RISK-01); local queue dev uses a local Redis container (ADR-0001), which still respects D-10.

decisions.title: Environment off except when working or presenting
decisions.decision: dev stays off except during work sessions and presentations.
decisions.why: Credits are limited; cost must follow use (E-07).
decisions.consequences: Needs an up/down procedure and an operator: make up / make down via Terraform switches (ADR-0004).

decisions.title: Paced admission: N buyers every T seconds
decisions.decision: The waiting room admits N buyers every T seconds, configurable.
decisions.why: Throttles load upstream of inventory (E-01/E-02).
decisions.consequences: Demo uses a large batch and a 5 s interval; parameters are service env vars (R-05).

decisions.title: Queue position over SSE, 3 s polling as plan B
decisions.decision: The queue position and admission travel to the browser over SSE; polling every 3 s is the fallback.
decisions.why: Push updates for the waiting room; polling costs about one hour if Cloud Run cuts streams.
decisions.consequences: queue needs CPU always allocated (ADR-0002) and streams up to 15 min; SSE is implemented (services/queue/src/queue/queue-stream.service.ts, apps/web/src/lib/sse.ts).

decisions.title: Schedule moves to Sept 28 - Oct 12
decisions.decision: Milestones rebased onto Mon Sept 28 - Mon Oct 12: contract freeze Tue Sept 29, milestones Fri Oct 2, Wed Oct 7, Fri Oct 9 (code freeze), submission Oct 12. About 10 h per person per week.
decisions.why: The Delivery 4 guide set the deadline on Oct 12 and asks for a written artifact.
decisions.consequences: Four extra working days, partly consumed by D-16..D-19. No load test in this slice.

decisions.title: Redis as a container on Cloud Run
decisions.decision: Run Redis as a Cloud Run container.
decisions.why: Original plan.
decisions.consequences: Impossible: Cloud Run has no raw TCP ingress. Superseded by ADR-0001 (Memorystore on demand).

decisions.title: Mock payment gateway as a Cloud Run function outside Orders
decisions.decision: functions/mock-payment-gateway is a Cloud Run function with its own contract; Orders reaches it only through its payment adapter (ACL); the browser reaches checkout via the Gateway (/mock-gateway/**); the 2 s delayed webhook is a Cloud Tasks task on queue payment-webhooks. Amended by D-21: still a function but no longer counted as a FaaS component.
decisions.why: Stands in for an external system and is stateless and short-lived, so the ACL and circuit breaker protect a real network hop. A function must finish work before responding, so the delay is a task, not a sleep.
decisions.alternatives: Convert a logic service to functions (rejected, contradicts Entrega 3 §5.2); ticket issuance as a function (rejected, new scope); pre-warmer (kept as alternative, chosen later in D-21).
decisions.consequences: One function, one Cloud Tasks queue, one more Gateway route target; optional Firestore payments collection (now declared in infra). Owner stays the Orders owner.

decisions.title: DLQ monitor as a FaaS component
decisions.decision: functions/dlq-monitor is triggered by the <subscription>-dlq topics (six since D-21) and writes one structured ERROR log per dead letter; a log-based metric and alert policy in Terraform fire when the count is > 0 within 5 minutes. make poison demonstrates it.
decisions.why: Second FaaS component with no new functional scope; realizes the E-05 tactic, which needs no load (one poison message is enough).
decisions.consequences: Adds an event-triggered function next to HTTP ones. Owner: Platform. Accepted by D-21 on 2026-10-03.

decisions.title: Timeouts, circuit breaker and retry on the payment path; fault injection in the mock
decisions.decision: Orders' payment adapter applies timeouts (0.5 s connect, 2 s response), a circuit breaker (opens after 5 consecutive failures, half-open after 30 s, fail <= 50 ms while open) and retry with exponential backoff 200 ms -> 5 s and jitter; open circuit returns 503 PAYMENT_UNAVAILABLE. The mock supports FAULT_MODE none|error|timeout via make fault.
decisions.why: Circuit Breaker is a Delivery 2 pattern and E-06 a Delivery 3 scenario; a timeout alone is hard to show live. Gives the demonstrable resilience tactic the guide requires.
decisions.consequences: New error code PAYMENT_UNAVAILABLE; small dependency (cockatiel, services/orders/src/payments/resilience.ts); reservation expiry is never extended; Orders runs one instance in dev so there is one breaker (ADR-0005).

decisions.title: Immutable artifacts and blue/green deployment
decisions.decision: Images tagged with the full git SHA and deployed by digest; function sources archived as <sha>.zip. Each release deploys a revision with --no-traffic --tag sha-<short>, smoke-tests the tag URL, then shifts 100 % (--to-latest); rollback shifts back. Migrations are expand/contract and run as a Cloud Run job before the shift; incompatible contract changes create /v2.
decisions.why: Guide requires an immutable artifact and a deliberate strategy; blue/green is verifiable before users see it and has one-command rollback.
decisions.alternatives: Rolling (Cloud Run default, not deliberate); canary (meaningless with demo traffic, optional step).
decisions.consequences: More pipeline work for Platform. Functions deploy all-at-once (no --no-traffic for functions) with rollback via traffic on their Cloud Run service. Observed: 3 min 6 s dispatch to 100 %, rollback 8.3 s (docs/evidence/deployment/README.md).

decisions.title: Inventory concurrency test is not cuttable
decisions.decision: The test of 200 concurrent reservations on 10 seats (expect exactly 10 created, 190 SOLD_OUT) stays; the first cut becomes the 'my orders' list screen.
decisions.why: It is the only running evidence of E-02, the scenario the inventory design exists for.
decisions.consequences: Inventory (lightest front) absorbs the work. Test lives in services/inventory/test/concurrency/.

decisions.title: FaaS components are the pre-warmer and the DLQ monitor
decisions.decision: functions/prewarmer (triggered by EventPublished, schedules warm/cool Cloud Tasks per event, sets service-level min instances on gateway and queue via the Cloud Run Admin API) and functions/dlq-monitor are the two FaaS components. The payment mock stays a function but is presented as a test double.
decisions.why: The professor required FaaS but not components added only to comply; both functions realize tactics Entrega 3 designed (E-01, E-05) on rare, short, stateless work.
decisions.alternatives: Convert a microservice (rejected: each keeps its Entrega 3 §5.2 container reason); ticket issuance consuming OrderPaid (rejected: new scope, nine days left).
decisions.consequences: E-01 becomes demonstrable. Terraform stops managing min_instance_count on gateway and queue (ADR-0004 amended). New Cloud Tasks queue prewarm-windows and a service account allowed to update only those two services.

decisions.title: Bring back queue-pass verification
decisions.decision: Proposed to sign the pass in Queue and verify it in Orders or Inventory if Milestone 2 (Oct 7) landed on time; the status doc records that pass verification stays out of scope.
decisions.why: D-07 is the largest deviation from the design (RD-04 not met) and estimated at two endpoints and half a day.
decisions.alternatives: Justify the deviation in the artifact using target-vs-slice.md (the path taken).
decisions.consequences: RD-04 remains unmet; deviation must be stated openly in the artifact and presentation.

decisions.title: All code-level names in English
decisions.decision: Code names are English; Spanish design names are mapped in docs/architecture/glossary.md (e.g. PedidoPagado -> OrderPaid).
decisions.why: Team rule 'everything in English'.
decisions.consequences: Spanish only in apps/web user-facing text.

decisions.title: Login sub is a UUID v5 of the lower-cased email
decisions.decision: The JWT sub is UUID v5 of the lower-cased email.
decisions.why: The same person must get the same userId on every login or 'my orders' and queue re-entry break.
decisions.consequences: Deterministic user ids without a user store.

decisions.title: Mock checkout completes via GET .../complete?outcome=
decisions.decision: The mock payment page completes with GET /mock-gateway/checkout/{paymentId}/complete?outcome=APPROVED|DECLINED.
decisions.why: The Gateway only routes GET /mock-gateway/**.

decisions.title: Extra error codes
decisions.decision: Adds NOT_FOUND (404), RATE_LIMITED (429), INVALID_SIGNATURE (401), PAYMENT_UNAVAILABLE (503), INTERNAL (500).
decisions.why: Needed by the plan's own behavior but missing from its table.

decisions.title: Admission parameters are env vars, not sales rules
decisions.decision: ADMISSION_BATCH_SIZE and ADMISSION_INTERVAL_SECONDS are queue service env vars.
decisions.why: Sales rules carry exactly three fields in the plan.
decisions.consequences: Changing pacing is a Terraform config change, not a catalog call.

decisions.title: Idempotent replay carries Idempotent-Replayed: true
decisions.decision: A response replayed from an Idempotency-Key has the header Idempotent-Replayed: true with the same status and body.
decisions.why: Makes replays observable in demo and logs; one line in the common interceptor.

decisions.title: Schema validation failures are 422 VALIDATION_ERROR
decisions.decision: Contract violations return 422 VALIDATION_ERROR; 400 is kept for malformed bodies and invalid Pub/Sub envelopes.
decisions.why: The request is well-formed JSON but breaks the contract (RFC 9110 §15.5.21); 400 on bad envelopes makes poison messages dead-letter.
decisions.consequences: Consumers must answer 400 (never 2xx) to poison messages (ADR-0005).

decisions.title: Queue store: Memorystore, created only for live tests and demos
decisions.decision: Queue store is Memorystore for Redis Basic 1 GB behind Terraform switch redis_enabled (default false), created by make redis-up and destroyed by make redis-down/down; private IP via DIRECT_PEERING on aforo-vpc, queue and gateway use Direct VPC egress, no AUTH/TLS. Amended 2026-10-05: gateway per-IP quota counters live in the same instance.
decisions.why: Cloud Run cannot reach a TCP Redis container (D-15); a sidecar would break statelessness. Entrega 3 (E-07, TO-02) already chose a managed store created per window by IaC because it bills by capacity.
decisions.alternatives: Redis container on Cloud Run (impossible); Redis sidecar in queue (one instance only, weakens statelessness).
decisions.consequences: ~US$1-2/day when on, zero when off; creation takes up to ~10 min and starts empty (seed rebuilds projection). Queue push subscriptions exist only while Redis is on. While off, queue answers 500 INTERNAL and the gateway quota is not enforced.

decisions.title: All work happens inside a request
decisions.decision: No service works after its response or on a timer: OutboxPublisher.flush() after commit and before responding; POST /internal/v1/housekeeping on catalog, inventory, orders called every minute by Cloud Scheduler (OIDC); payment webhook processed synchronously; queue is the only exception, with an in-process admission tick guarded by a Redis lock.
decisions.why: Cloud Run throttles CPU between requests and may stop idle instances, so pollers and respond-then-process would stall or be lost; always-on CPU everywhere costs money and hides the issue.
decisions.alternatives: CPU always allocated on every service (rejected: cost, E-07).
decisions.consequences: Failed publishes are at most one minute late; outbox-writing requests are tens of ms slower; webhook answers after processing (Cloud Tasks retries on non-2xx); only queue pays for always-allocated CPU.

decisions.title: Reservation expiry has a safety net
decisions.decision: Keep the Cloud Tasks expiry task (named by reservationId) and add a one-minute housekeeping sweep; expire is UPDATE ... WHERE status = 'ACTIVE' AND expires_at <= now(); a no-op returns 200 with the current state.
decisions.why: Commit-then-enqueue is a dual write: a lost task would block seats forever. Entrega 2 §5.4 requires the expiry instant to be reached.
decisions.alternatives: Outbox for tasks or an extra table (not needed).
decisions.consequences: A lost task delays expiry by at most one minute. Confirm and expire still race on the same conditional update; the time condition only makes expire lose more often. Observed: 10 reservations expired by Cloud Tasks at the TTL, seats 0 -> 10, orders EXPIRED (docs/evidence/reliability-expiry/README.md).

decisions.title: Terraform owns configuration, CI owns code and traffic
decisions.decision: Terraform owns every resource, env, secrets, scaling, probes, IAM; CI owns images/function sources and traffic (Terraform ignore_changes on image, traffic, function source). Runtime switches env_on, redis_enabled, mock_fault_mode change only via make, read back from Terraform outputs. Probes use /health/live. Amended 2026-10-03 by D-21: prewarmer owns min instances of gateway and queue.
decisions.why: Two tools change the same Cloud Run services; without a split, apply reverts CI deploys or CI overwrites config. gcloud-based switches would violate 'nothing outside IaC'.
decisions.alternatives: gcloud-based make fault / up / down (original plan).
decisions.consequences: No drift; make fault takes ~1 min. Config changes go live all-at-once, only code is blue/green. Functions have no pre-traffic smoke test.

decisions.title: Dev sizing and demo determinism
decisions.decision: Connection budget 19 of 22 via instance caps x DB_POOL_MAX (inventory 3x2, orders 1x3, catalog 2x2, migrate 1, devs 5); gateway max 3, web 2, queue 2, functions 5 (prewarmer 1, concurrency 1); all min 0. Orders runs one instance. Push subscriptions retry 10-60 s, max 5 attempts, DLQ each; consumers answer 400 to invalid envelopes; alert evaluates over 60 s.
decisions.why: db-f1-micro allows 25 connections; an in-memory breaker across several Orders instances makes E-06 non-deterministic; default Pub/Sub backoff could miss the 5 min E-05 target.
decisions.consequences: E-02 aggregate concurrency limit becomes visible config. Limits are demo-sized, not load-test-sized. Local runs must set DB_POOL_MAX=1. Orders cannot scale out in dev.

decisions.title: Inventory not sharded; event_id is the partition key
decisions.decision: Inventory stays on one database; if sharding is needed the key is event_id. Every Inventory table carries event_id and main keys/indexes start with it.
decisions.why: Entrega 3 TO-03 names sharding by event as the way out; event_id keeps the sector counter, reservation and per-buyer limit in one local ACID transaction.
decisions.alternatives: user_id (splits the counter), reservation_id (scatter-gather), created_at (temporal hotspot).
decisions.consequences: Nothing to build now. One very large event remains a single-node hotspot; admission control helps, sharding does not.

decisions.title: Frontend framework: Next.js instead of Angular
decisions.decision: apps/web is Next.js (App Router, TypeScript); SSR only on / and /events/[id]; UI from shadcn/ui on Radix and Tailwind. Accepted 2026-10-07 by Julián.
decisions.why: apps/web had no code yet and the team building screens works in React; no Angular-specific feature is needed.
decisions.consequences: No NEXT_PUBLIC_* vars (image configured at runtime; API_BASE_URL handed via root layout); web exposes its own /health/live and /health/ready; Terraform and CI unchanged (port 4000).

decisions.title: Design requirement: only admitted buyers can reserve
decisions.decision: Entrega 2 requirement that the waiting room be a system control; not met in the slice.
decisions.why: Depends on pass verification, cut by D-07.
decisions.consequences: Any valid session can call /orders without going through the queue.

decisions.title: Route prefixes and /v2 for breaking changes
decisions.decision: Public endpoints under /api/v1, internal under /internal/v1 (never exposed by the Gateway); an incompatible change creates /v2 or event version 2 served in parallel, never modifying v1 (RD-05).
decisions.why: Lets providers and consumers deploy independently.
decisions.consequences: Compatible changes ship provider first, then consumers (build-and-deploy.md).

decisions.title: Logic services trust Gateway identity headers
decisions.decision: The Gateway validates the bearer token and forwards X-User-Id and X-User-Email; no logic service validates the user token again. Service-to-service calls use Cloud Run IAM with Google OIDC ID tokens.
decisions.why: Only the Gateway can invoke the private services, so re-validation adds nothing in the slice.
decisions.consequences: Security depends on Cloud Run IAM invoker bindings. AUTH_MODE=dev accepts a fake token locally.

decisions.title: Correlation ID across HTTP, bus and tasks
decisions.decision: The Gateway generates X-Correlation-Id if absent; every service forwards it, logs it, and publishes it in every envelope and Pub/Sub attribute; Cloud Tasks requests carry it too.
decisions.why: E-05: follow one purchase across services in Cloud Logging.
decisions.consequences: One correlationId observed across gateway, orders, inventory and prewarmer in evidence runs.

decisions.title: Idempotency-Key on every state-changing operation
decisions.decision: Every state-changing operation carries Idempotency-Key; the service stores key, body hash and response; a repeat returns the same response (RD-02); same key with a different body is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. The frontend generates one key per user attempt.
decisions.why: Retries (client, Cloud Tasks, Pub/Sub) must not duplicate orders or charges.
decisions.consequences: Implemented once in @aforo/common; replay observed in docs/evidence/fails-well.

decisions.title: Errors are application/problem+json with a fixed code table
decisions.decision: All errors are application/problem+json with type, title, status, code, detail, correlationId; codes come from a fixed table; detail is never parsed by clients.
decisions.why: One error shape across services and the UI.

decisions.title: Default timeouts on every outgoing call
decisions.decision: Every outgoing call has a timeout, default connect 0.5 s, response 2 s.
decisions.why: Kept tactic from Entrega 3 (scope.md).
decisions.consequences: The Gateway overrides it for long hops (see ST-05).

decisions.title: Health endpoints and probes
decisions.decision: GET /health/live and /health/ready without auth; Cloud Run probes call only /health/live; smoke tests check /health/ready.
decisions.why: A service must deploy and boot even when its DB or Redis is off (ADR-0004).

decisions.title: Data formats
decisions.decision: ISO-8601 UTC dates, money as integer cents + currency COP, UUID v4 string ids, 0-based pagination, camelCase JSON, UPPER_SNAKE_CASE enums, snake_case columns.
decisions.why: Shared conventions avoid integration bugs.

decisions.title: Delivery 2 patterns realized in the slice
decisions.decision: API Gateway, Database per Service, orchestrated Saga in Orders, Transactional Outbox/Inbox, idempotent consumer, idempotency key, Anti-Corruption Layer (orders payments adapter), Circuit Breaker, delayed delivery/competing expiry, health checks.
decisions.why: Guide requires Delivery 2 styles and patterns visible in code and deployment.
decisions.consequences: Microservices plus event-driven style via Pub/Sub push subscriptions.

decisions.title: Compute model per unit: containers vs FaaS
decisions.decision: gateway, web, queue, catalog, orders, inventory are Cloud Run containers; prewarmer and dlq-monitor are FaaS; mock-payment-gateway is a function presented as a test double.
decisions.why: Lab 5 criteria: services have continuous traffic, SSE streams or DB pools (Entrega 3 §5.2); the functions do rare, millisecond, stateless work.
decisions.consequences: Functions follow Lab 5's five phases (granularity, contract, externalized state, idempotency, timeouts).

decisions.title: Two persistence paradigms
decisions.decision: Relational Cloud SQL PostgreSQL for catalog, orders, inventory, and in-memory key-value with sorted sets (Memorystore) for the queue. Firestore is used by the payment mock.
decisions.why: Guide asks for multiple persistence paradigms; each store matches its owner's access pattern.
decisions.consequences: Firestore was optional in D-16 and is declared in infra/envs/dev/functions.tf; delivery-4.md lists only the two paradigms.

decisions.title: One purchase path only; acceptance script defines scope
decisions.decision: Only login -> catalog -> waiting room -> reserve -> mock payment -> paid order is built; nothing enters scope unless it is in docs/plan/acceptance.md. Covers RF-01..05, RF-08..12, orders half of RF-14; RF-06 partial; RF-07, RF-13, RF-15..26 out.
decisions.why: Delivery is judged on a complete working prototype, not design coverage.
decisions.consequences: Managed identity, pass verification, edge/WAF/CAPTCHA, ticket issuance, notifications and gate validation are out.

decisions.title: Load-only tactics dropped
decisions.decision: Multi-zone replica, window-sized DB profile, error-rate alerts and load tests are dropped.
decisions.why: They are only verifiable under load, not in a functional demo.
decisions.consequences: E-03 shows health checks only; E-02 uses dev sizing instead of a 100-connection profile.

decisions.title: No global load balancer, CDN or Cloud Armor
decisions.decision: Browser hits the Gateway directly; the Gateway applies a per-IP quota (Redis-backed).
decisions.why: Target L7 LB + CDN + WAF per window is out of the slice.
decisions.consequences: Way back: add the LB in Terraform in front of web and gateway.

decisions.title: Identity Platform replaced by Gateway-issued JWT
decisions.decision: Gateway issues HS256 JWT with OIDC claims instead of Identity Platform validated against JWKS.
decisions.why: See D-06.
decisions.consequences: Way back: replace token validation in the Gateway and drop /auth/login.

decisions.title: Opaque queue pass instead of ES256-signed pass
decisions.decision: Opaque token in Redis, forwarded as X-Queue-Pass, never verified.
decisions.why: See D-07.
decisions.consequences: Way back: sign in Queue, verify in Orders/Inventory (two endpoints, half a day).

decisions.title: Memorystore Basic without replica
decisions.decision: Memorystore Basic (no replica), created only for live tests and demos.
decisions.why: Cost; see ADR-0001.
decisions.consequences: Way back: Standard tier in Terraform.

decisions.title: One small single-zone Cloud SQL instead of window profile with standby
decisions.decision: One db-f1-micro, three databases, single zone, 25 connections split by instance caps x pools.
decisions.why: Cost and demo-sized traffic (ADR-0005).
decisions.consequences: No failover; E-02 burst p95 missed on dev. Way back: Terraform profile.

decisions.title: VPC used only for Memorystore
decisions.decision: One VPC used only for queue/gateway to Memorystore (Direct VPC egress); Cloud Run privacy via IAM; Cloud SQL via connector. No NAT, no internal ingress for logic services.
decisions.why: Simplify networking for the slice.
decisions.consequences: Way back: extend the VPC to every service and add NAT.

decisions.title: Wompi replaced by a mock function
decisions.decision: Mock payment gateway as a Cloud Run function; Orders' adapter keeps circuit breaker, timeouts, retries.
decisions.consequences: Way back: implement a Wompi adapter.

decisions.title: Logs + DLQ alert only; no tracing or metrics alerts
decisions.decision: Structured JSON logs with correlation ID + DLQ alert via dlq-monitor.
decisions.why: Error-rate alerts and tracing are only meaningful under load.
decisions.consequences: Way back: OpenTelemetry and error-rate alerts.

decisions.title: Pre-warming at minimum 1, multi-zone and load tests dropped
decisions.decision: Pre-warming kept with minimum 1 instead of 2-3 and warm for at most 1 h; connection cap kept as dev sizing; multi-zone and load tests dropped.
decisions.why: Demo-sized environment and cost.
decisions.consequences: Way back: raise warm minimums in TARGET_SERVICES.

decisions.title: Platform took over catalog, inventory and finishing orders
decisions.decision: The Platform owner took over catalog, inventory and finishing orders.
decisions.why: Not stated (schedule pressure implied).

decisions.title: Catalog behavior the contract left open
decisions.decision: Publishing twice emits nothing the second time; a list without status includes drafts; no organizer roles.
decisions.why: Contract did not specify these; consistent with D-06 and D-08.
decisions.consequences: Documented in the catalog README.

decisions.title: Seed dates are fixed
decisions.decision: Seeded events use fixed dates, so the prewarmer skips them.
decisions.why: Re-running the seed (every make up/redis-up) must not schedule warm windows.
decisions.consequences: E-01 demos create a new event each run; catalog has no delete, so demo events accumulate.

decisions.title: Gateway timeouts above the convention
decisions.decision: Gateway upstream timeouts: orders 15 s, mock pages 10 s, queue 8 s.
decisions.why: Orders' payment path can take ~6.5 s with retries; a cold queue took ~3.2 s vs a 2.5 s gateway timeout (#40).
decisions.consequences: Deviates from the default timeouts in contracts/conventions.md.

decisions.title: E-02 on dev runs through the gateway
decisions.decision: The E-02 dev run sends orders as buyers through the public gateway, not directly to inventory.
decisions.why: No service-account token needed and it exercises the real path.
decisions.consequences: It skips the waiting room because the pass is not verified (D-07).

decisions.title: Always open the web at its run.app URL
decisions.decision: Use https://aforo-web-68220265740.southamerica-east1.run.app for the web.
decisions.why: CORS is configured for that origin.
decisions.consequences: Other URL forms of the same service fail CORS.

decisions.title: No local environment slows the loop
decisions.decision: Mitigation: unit and service tests locally against Prism mocks; cloud is for integration. Likelihood high.
decisions.why: Consequence of D-10.

decisions.title: Shared environment broken by one person
decisions.decision: Mitigation: nobody deploys without green CI; whoever breaks main fixes it first. Likelihood high.
decisions.why: One shared dev (D-04).

decisions.title: Environment left on eats credits
decisions.decision: Mitigation: make down mandatory when done; check billing every Friday. Likelihood medium.

decisions.title: make down leaves no data
decisions.decision: Mitigation: the seed is idempotent and always runs inside make up. Likelihood medium.

decisions.title: Contracts change after the freeze
decisions.decision: Mitigation: only the contracts owner edits them; late changes announced the same day and versioned. Likelihood high.

decisions.title: Cloud Run cuts the queue SSE
decisions.decision: Mitigation: plan B polls status every 3 s with the same contract. Likelihood medium.

decisions.title: Memorystore is slow to create and starts empty
decisions.decision: Mitigation: make redis-up >= 15 min before any live test; it re-runs the seed; positions rebuild on re-join. Likelihood high.

decisions.title: Direct VPC egress unavailable in the region
decisions.decision: Mitigation: check on day one; fallback Serverless VPC Access connector under the same switch. Likelihood low.

decisions.title: Manual terraform apply resets switches
decisions.decision: Mitigation: only make targets apply, reading current switches from state. Likelihood medium.

decisions.title: Background work stalls on Cloud Run
decisions.decision: Mitigation: no timers or post-response work outside queue; outbox flush after commit + housekeeping. Likelihood medium.

decisions.title: Integration piles up at the end
decisions.decision: Mitigation: two fixed integration points (Wed Sept 30, Mon Oct 5) with real deploys. Likelihood high.

decisions.title: Someone drops out
decisions.decision: Mitigation: redistribute fronts; cut the 'my orders' list screen first. Likelihood medium.
decisions.consequences: In practice Platform took over catalog, inventory and orders (ST-01).

decisions.title: Delivery 4 requirements not visible in the running system
decisions.decision: Mitigation: tracked item by item in delivery-4.md; rehearsed Thu Oct 8. Likelihood medium.

decisions.title: nodejs24 functions runtime not available in region
decisions.decision: Mitigation: fall back to nodejs22 for the functions only. Likelihood low.

decisions.title: Elasticity: pre-warming per sales window
decisions.decision: Target: entry path has instances running when a sale opens, scales to zero otherwise. Tactic: prewarmer sets min instances of gateway and queue to 1 (lead 600 s, hold up to 3600 s), plus autoscaling, scale to zero, admission throttling, per-IP quota.
decisions.why: Opening time is known from the catalog, so capacity can be ready before the spike without paying when idle.
decisions.consequences: Observed Oct 9: gateway and queue 0 -> 1 three seconds after publishing; queue join at the opening 550 ms vs 4 070 ms cold; back to 0 at the close (docs/evidence/e01-prewarming). Prewarmer covers only sales windows; first join after an idle pause can still be cold.

decisions.title: Zero overselling
decisions.decision: Target: overselling = 0; p95 reservation <= 300 ms. Tactic: serialized conditional write in inventory, admission control upstream, aggregate concurrency limit = instance caps x DB pools (ADR-0005).
decisions.why: The inventory design exists for this scenario (D-20).
decisions.consequences: Observed on dev Oct 9 through the gateway: 200 buyers on 10 seats -> 10 created, 190 SOLD_OUT, 0 oversold. Inventory p95 808 ms all at once (target missed), 75 ms metered at 20/s. Local run p95 169 ms.

decisions.title: Availability
decisions.decision: Tactic in the slice: health checks; Cloud Run spreads instances across zones.
decisions.why: Only health checks are demonstrable without load.
decisions.consequences: Health checks only; no evidence folder for E-03.

decisions.title: Observability: dead-lettered message raises an alert
decisions.decision: Target: DLQ alert <= 5 min; purchase traceable by correlationId. Tactic: structured logs + correlation ID across HTTP and bus; dlq-monitor logs dead letters; log-based metric and alert policy email the team.
decisions.why: Needs no load: one poison message is enough.
decisions.consequences: Observed Oct 9: poison message rejected 5 times by each of 3 consumers, 3 DLQs, dlq-monitor logged at +1 min 36 s, incident and email at +3 min 30 s. Incident auto-closes 30 min later, not at once.

decisions.title: Payment gateway resilience
decisions.decision: Target: fail fast <= 50 ms with the circuit open; 0 double charges; recover without a deploy. Tactic: timeouts, circuit breaker, retry with backoff and jitter, no expiry extension; fault injected with make fault MODE=timeout.
decisions.why: Live, demonstrable resilience tactic required by the guide (D-18).
decisions.consequences: Observed Oct 9 03:28-03:33 UTC: 503 PAYMENT_UNAVAILABLE, circuit opened on the 5th failed attempt, open-circuit failures ~10 ms in orders, closed after fault removed. Half-open probe re-opened once on a cold mock instance (2.8 s > 2 s); the timed-out probe still created a payment in the mock.

decisions.title: Cost follows use
decisions.decision: Target: near-zero cost when idle, only demo resources during demos, one command on/off. Tactic: scale to zero, make down, Memorystore created per window by IaC (make redis-up).
decisions.why: Credits are limited (D-11); Entrega 3 E-07.
decisions.consequences: Switch behavior documented and post-make down state verified Oct 9 (Cloud SQL STOPPED, no Redis, schedulers paused, minScale 0). Billing screenshots still pending.

decisions.title: Security
decisions.decision: Tactic in the slice: private Cloud Run + IAM invoker, Gateway token check, HMAC webhook, input validation. Partially demonstrable.
decisions.consequences: No evidence folder; queue pass not verified (D-07).

decisions.title: Deployment evidence: blue/green, migration, rollback
decisions.decision: Target: immutable artifact and deliberate strategy with rollback. Run: make deploy SERVICE=orders -> migrate job -> no-traffic revision -> smoke on tag URL -> shift.
decisions.consequences: Observed: 3 min 6 s dispatch to 100 %; rollback 8.3 s, roll forward 5.6 s; an orders image that could not boot (#38) never got traffic.

decisions.title: Queue pass forwarded and logged but never verified
decisions.decision: X-Queue-Pass is forwarded and logged but never verified downstream.
decisions.consequences: RD-04 not met.

decisions.title: Login simulated by the Gateway
decisions.decision: Login is an HS256 JWT issued by the Gateway with no password.

decisions.title: No Edge/CDN/WAF/CAPTCHA
decisions.decision: The browser talks directly to the Gateway; no managed edge, CDN, WAF or CAPTCHA.
decisions.why: Out of the slice.

decisions.title: No ticket issuance
decisions.decision: Ticket issuance is not built.
decisions.why: New functional scope (RF-15+).

decisions.title: No notifications
decisions.decision: Notifications (with their queue and DLQ) are entirely out.
decisions.why: Not in the acceptance script.

decisions.title: Payment gateway is a mock with fault injection
decisions.decision: The payment gateway is a Cloud Run function test double with deliberate fault injection, not one of the FaaS components.

decisions.title: OrderPaid published but not consumed
decisions.decision: OrderPaid is published through the outbox but has no subscriber.
decisions.why: Ticket issuance and notifications are out.
decisions.consequences: Way back: add a subscriber, no change in Orders.

notes: Contradictions and caveats: (1) docs/plan/delivery-4.md#L24 claims 'contract tests in CI against deployed revisions'; CI only runs Redocly lint (.github/workflows/contracts.yml) and service workflows run lint/test/docker build; docs/status/2026-10-08-missing.md#L122 says it was not built. build-and-deploy.md also lists 'contract tests against Prism' on PR and a '+ contract check' in the smoke step, but the smoke checks only /health/ready. (2) D-18, D-19, D-20 are still 'Proposed' in docs/plan/delivery-4-decisions.md#L17-19 and decisions.md#L26 ('Proposed, confirm as a team'), though all are implemented and evidenced; recorded here as accepted. D-16 table row also says Proposed but is amended by D-21. (3) docs/architecture/build-and-deploy.md#L3 says 'Status: design - to be implemented in CI' but docs/evidence/deployment shows it running. (4) D-16/overview.md call the Firestore payments collection optional; infra/envs/dev/functions.tf#L174 declares a Firestore database, so it was adopted; delivery-4.md persistence row lists only Postgres + Redis. (5) The Open decision on pass verification (delivery-4-decisions.md#L238) still reads 'Open'; status missing.md#L135 says it stays out of scope (recorded as D-07-open, dropped). (6) E-02 target p95 <= 300 ms was missed on dev under a simultaneous burst (808 ms) and met only when metered (75 ms). (7) delivery-4.md marks E-07 demonstrable via billing dashboard, but billing screenshots are pending. (8) Status doc says a '2.5 s convention' for gateway timeouts; contracts/conventions.md#L89 states 2 s response default. (9) D-18 says retry 'with jitter'; the E-06 evidence does not mention jitter; code uses cockatiel ExponentialBackoff (services/orders/src/payments/resilience.ts), whose default generator is decorrelated jitter (library default, not explicit config). (10) risks.md has no IDs; RISK-01..14 are assigned here in file order. Target-vs-slice rows use TVS-*, convention rules CONV-*, status-doc decisions ST-* (ST-04 skipped intentionally, ADR-0007 already covered), gaps GAP-*. RD-02 and RD-05 are folded into CONV-idempotency and CONV-versioning. New component ids used: sched-housekeeping. (11) There is no E-04 in the tactic map. (12) D-12/R-05 admission pacing and the queue's in-process timer are an explicit ADR-0002 exception to the 'no timers' rule in CLAUDE.md.
